full_judgment:
2. The respondents as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 86 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bhurungamari, Kurigram for partition. Their case, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian Nos. 60/1, and 833 of Char Bhurungamari Mouza, C.S. Khatian No. 84 of Bhurungamari Mouza originally belonged to Sutai Sheikh, Monoruddin Sheikh Sonoruddin Sheikh and Babuillah to the extent of 3 annas and 12 gondas share each and Nilmoti alias Niljan to the extent of 1 anna and 12 gondas. After that, Babuilla died leaving behind his two brothers, namely, Monoruddin Sheikh and Snoruddin Sheikh and sister Nilmati alias Niljan and Sonoruddin died leaving behind three sons, namely, Khaimuddin, Moimuddin and Shanu and Shanu died leaving behind his two brothers, namely, Khaimuddin and Noimuddin. Plaintiff Nos. 1-5 are the heirs of Sutai Sheikh, plaintiff Nos. 6-9 are the heirs of Monoruddin Sheikh and plaintiff Nos. 10-12 are the heirs of Khaimuddin. Defendant Nos. 13-20 purchased share from the heirs of Monoruddin and Sonoruddin, Milmati alias Niljan sold 1.25 acres of land to Safaruddin and others and 1.25 acres of land to Khaiuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of plaintiff Nos. 10-12. In this way, the plaintiffs acquired title in 21.64 acres out of 34.98 acres of land as described in the schedule to the plaint, Lastly, the plaintiffs requested the defendants to effect the partition of the suit land on 19.10.1986 but the defendants denied. Consequently, the cause of action of the suit arose. At the time of R.S. operation, the name of the predecessor-in-interest of defendant No. 2 was recorded in Khatian Nos. 132 and 134. The name of Kotwal Sheikh, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 3-10 was recorded in Khatian No. 131. The names of the predecessors-in-interest of defendant Nos. 11-13 and defendant Nos. 13-21 were recorded in Khatian No. 97. The names of defendant Nos. 27-49 have been recorded in Khatian No. 83 Those records of right were prepared erroneously. Hence the suit for partition has been filed by the plaintiffs. 

 9. Having considered the findings of the trial Court, the High Court Division came to a finding that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their title to and possession in the suit land and that the appellate Court without considering the oral evidence as to possession erroneously reversed the finding of the trial Court. The High Court Division further found that the names of the heirs of C.S. recorded tenants had been recorded in S.A. Khatian Nos. 130, 131, 133 and 129 and that the land recorded in CS Khatian No. 60/1 had been recorded in those Khatians and also in Khatian Nos. 134, 97 and 61 during S.A. operation. The High Court Division, therefore, came to a finding that on the facts and in circumstances of the case, it could not be said that the names of the C.S. recorded tenants or their successive heirs had not at all been recorded during S.A. operation in corresponding S.A. khatians.
